This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from PAGASA and international models indicate a likely daily high of 33–34°C in Metro Manila on May 19, driven by typical late-dry-season solar heating peaking in the afternoon before any convective clouds or isolated showers develop. Historical May averages for the city hover near 33–34°C, with urban heat-island effects at official stations occasionally pushing readings one degree higher amid light winds and high humidity. Trader consensus around the 34°C outcome reflects this narrow window, tempered by uncertainty over whether afternoon thunderstorms—common this time of year—will arrive early enough to cap temperatures at 33°C or allow brief clearing that supports a 35°C peak. Updated PAGASA outlooks and real-time station data expected in the next 48 hours will likely sharpen resolution criteria.
